final_rationale: The verdict does not change because no new admissible evidence was received. The Actor appropriately narrowed the claim and conceded the core weakness, but that clarification does not satisfy the governing policy condition. Admissible evidence still shows that the affected named use case remains exposed, the segment is below target, and there is no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure. Under the stated policy, rollout controls and monitoring can support a reversible launch posture, but they do not remove the disclosure duty or substitute for approved risk acceptance when the affected segment remains in scope. That means the caveat is not merely a disclosure nuance; it is an unresolved compliance predicate. Some evidence supports operational readiness, so the record is not purely noncompliant, but the certification claim remains suspicious on the model-card disclosure question.
remaining_concerns: The small-business onboarding segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort despite being below target on long-context onboarding support.
The policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The available risk-acceptance document is only a draft, has no approver signature, and does not mention the exposed small-business onboarding segment.
A 6% rollout, rollback switch, and monitoring support operational readiness but do not satisfy the disclosure-policy predicate while the affected use case remains exposed.
The Actor's narrower framing is a reinterpretation of the same evidence, not new admissible evidence curing the unresolved compliance condition.
